ELUCIDATION
ON
REGIONAL REGULATION OF PURBALINGGA REGENCY
NUMBER 2 YEAR 2017
CONCERNING
THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR VICTIMS OF
GENDER-BASED VIOLENCE AND CHILDREN

I. GENERAL
Cases of gender-based violence and violence against children have recently been increasing, both in number and in the forms and modus operandi which are becoming more diverse. Rape, sexual harassment, domestic violence, sexual exploitation, violence against domestic workers, pornography, and neglect can occur in private, community, and public domains.

Various causes of gender-based violence and violence against children include legal instruments that have not been able to provide protection to victims, the role of media that is less supportive in reporting on gender-based violence and violence against children, public services that are not yet optimal, poverty issues, erroneous interpretation of religious teachings, all of which cannot be separated from the strong patriarchal culture in society.

Therefore, victims of gender-based violence and violence against children need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality, and upholding human rights. This Regional Regulation regulates the Implementation of Protection for Victims of Gender-Based Violence and Children, particularly in terms of prevention and services, protection mechanisms, community participation, guidance, funding, and supervision.

CHAPTER I
GENERAL PROVISIONS
Article 1
In this Regional Regulation, what is meant by: Region is Purbalingga Regency.
Regional Government is the Regional Head as an element of regional government administration who leads the implementation of government affairs that are the authority of the autonomous region.
Regent is the Regent of Purbalingga.
District is a part of the Regency Region led by a District Head.
District Head is the leader of the District who is under and responsible to the Regent through the Regional Secretary.
Regional Apparatus is the Regional Apparatus that administers affairs in the Field of Women's Empowerment and Child Protection.
Child is a person who has not yet reached the age of 18 (eighteen) years, including a child still in the womb.
Gender is a concept that refers to the roles and responsibilities of men and women that occur as a result of and can be changed by the social and cultural conditions of society.
Protection is all efforts aimed at providing a sense of security and fulfilling the rights of victims carried out by family members, integrated services, advocates, social institutions, police, prosecutors, courts, or other parties either temporarily or based on court determination.
Child Protection is all activities to guarantee and protect children and their rights so that they can live, grow, develop, and participate optimally in accordance with human dignity and worth, and receive protection from violence and discrimination.
Implementation of Protection is a series of activities aimed at preventing the occurrence of violence, providing protection and recovery services and social reintegration, conducting coordination and cooperation, and increasing community participation carried out by the Integrated Service Center.
Gender-Based Violence is any form of restriction, exclusion, differentiation and all forms of treatment carried out on the basis of gender and aimed at reducing, eliminating the recognition, enjoyment or use of human rights, the consequences of which are in the form of and not limited to physical, sexual, psychological and economic violence.
Violence Against Children is any form of restriction, differentiation, exclusion and all forms of treatment carried out against children, the consequences of which are in the form of and not limited to physical, sexual, psychological, and economic violence.
Victim of Gender-Based Violence is a person who due to their gender experiences physical, psychological, economic, social, sexual suffering, and other losses resulting from state policies, acts of violence and/or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community.
Child Victim of Violence is a child who receives harsh treatment either physically, psychologically, economically, socially, sexually, and other losses resulting from state policies, acts of violence and/or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community.
Victim Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of gender-based violence and children to be more empowered, whether physically, psychologically, socially, economically or sexually.
Companion is a Social Worker who has professional competence in their field.
Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the purpose of self-strengthening of victims of gender-based violence and children to resolve the problems they face.
Social Reintegration is the process of preparing victims and communities that support the reunification of victims into a family environment or family substitute that can provide protection and fulfillment of the victim's needs.
Safe House is a temporary residence used to provide protection for victims of gender-based violence and children in accordance with determined operational standards.
Regional Action Plan is the foundation and guideline for regional apparatus, vertical agencies, and the community in carrying out activities for the implementation of protection for victims of gender-based violence and children.
Integrated Service Center for Protection of Victims of Gender-Based Violence and Children hereinafter abbreviated as PPT PKBGA is a special service place for victims of gender-based violence and children carried out cross-functionally and cross-sectorally as one unit of implementation so that victims receive maximum service in an integrated and comprehensive manner.
Complaint Service Unit at District Level hereinafter abbreviated as UPPTK is a special service place for victims of gender-based violence and children located at the district level so that victims receive maximum service in an integrated and comprehensive manner.

Article 18
Monitoring and Reporting as referred to in Article 9 letter i constitutes activities that include monitoring, documenting and reporting cases of gender-based and child violence.

2.3.rationale: In the Indonesian source, Pasal 18 explicitly states: "Monitoring dan Pelaporan ... meliputi memonitor, mendokumentasikan dan melaporkan kasus kekerasan berbasis gender dan anak." This is an explicit case documentation/reporting mechanism (at least a basic information system function for case data). The retrieved English candidate [2.3-31] contains this content, and the judge’s reasoning (that this constitutes a data/documentation system for cases) is reasonable. Therefore the disagreement is best explained by a likely issue with the golden label being coded as No (too strict a definition of 'information system' beyond monitoring/documenting/reporting), rather than missing evidence. If the indicator requires a formal database/IT system, the policy does not specify IT, but it does specify systematic documentation/reporting; under many rubrics that should still be Yes.

Article 2
Letter a What is meant by the principle of "non-discrimination" is protection for all victims of gender-based violence and children without distinguishing ethnicity, religion, race, class, gender, ethnic group, culture, language, legal status and physical or mental condition.

Letter c What is meant by the principle of "gender justice" is fair treatment given to women and men.

5.3.rationale: The Indonesian text does not clearly mandate engagement with traditional/customary (adat) institutions or leaders. Pasal 17 only says "menumbuhkan kearifan lokal" (fostering local wisdom) in handling cases, which is a cultural framing but not explicit collaboration with traditional/cultural organizations/leaders. Pasal 27 lists community actors (tokoh agama, tokoh masyarakat appear in UPPTK membership in Pasal 19; and 'lembaga keagamaan' etc. in Pasal 27(3)), but nothing specifically about adat/traditional institutions. Given that, the judge’s No is defensible based on the retrieved passages (which include Pasal 17). This suggests the golden label Yes may be over-inclusive (treating 'kearifan lokal' as sufficient evidence of traditional/cultural engagement). If the rubric indeed counts 'kearifan lokal' alone as traditional/cultural engagement, then the judge was too strict; but based on the policy text, explicit engagement with traditional/cultural leaders is not stated.

6.5.rationale: The Indonesian source (Penjelasan Pasal 2 huruf a) defines non-discrimination as protection without distinguishing "... status hukum dan kondisi fisik maupun mental." This is a general non-discrimination clause and does not specifically mention disability (disabilitas/penyandang disabilitas) or disability-specific measures/accommodations. The judge inferred that 'physical or mental condition' implicitly covers persons with disabilities and therefore answered Yes. If the indicator 'Disability' requires explicit mention or targeted provisions for persons with disabilities, that inference is too lenient. Since the relevant text was present in the retrieved candidates and translation is faithful, the error is primarily the judge’s over-broad interpretation rather than retrieval/translation.

Victim of Gender-Based Violence is a person who due to their gender experiences physical, psychological, economic, social, sexual suffering, and other losses resulting from state policies, acts of violence and/or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community.
Child Victim of Violence is a child who receives harsh treatment either physically, psychologically, economically, socially, sexually, and other losses resulting from state policies, acts of violence and/or threats of violence within the scope of the household and community.
Victim Recovery is all efforts to strengthen victims of gender-based violence and children to be more empowered, whether physically, psychologically, socially, economically or sexually.
Companion is a Social Worker who has professional competence in their field.
Assistance is all actions in the form of counseling, psychological therapy, advocacy, and spiritual guidance, for the purpose of self-strengthening of victims of gender-based violence and children to resolve the problems they face.
Social Reintegration is the process of preparing victims and communities that support the reunification of victims into a family environment or family substitute that can provide protection and fulfillment of the victim's needs.
Safe House is a temporary residence used to provide protection for victims of gender-based violence and children in accordance with determined operational standards.
Regional Action Plan is the foundation and guideline for regional apparatus, vertical agencies, and the community in carrying out activities for the implementation of protection for victims of gender-based violence and children.
Integrated Service Center for Protection of Victims of Gender-Based Violence and Children hereinafter abbreviated as PPT PKBGA is a special service place for victims of gender-based violence and children carried out cross-functionally and cross-sectorally as one unit of implementation so that victims receive maximum service in an integrated and comprehensive manner.
Complaint Service Unit at District Level hereinafter abbreviated as UPPTK is a special service place for victims of gender-based violence and children located at the district level so that victims receive maximum service in an integrated and comprehensive manner.

Article 5
The Implementation of Protection for Victims of Gender-Based Violence and Children, is carried out by: PPT PKBGA; and

ELUCIDATION
ON
REGIONAL REGULATION OF PURBALINGGA REGENCY
NUMBER 2 YEAR 2017
CONCERNING
THE IMPLEMENTATION OF PROTECTION FOR VICTIMS OF
GENDER-BASED VIOLENCE AND CHILDREN

I. GENERAL
Cases of gender-based violence and violence against children have recently been increasing, both in number and in the forms and modus operandi which are becoming more diverse. Rape, sexual harassment, domestic violence, sexual exploitation, violence against domestic workers, pornography, and neglect can occur in private, community, and public domains.

Various causes of gender-based violence and violence against children include legal instruments that have not been able to provide protection to victims, the role of media that is less supportive in reporting on gender-based violence and violence against children, public services that are not yet optimal, poverty issues, erroneous interpretation of religious teachings, all of which cannot be separated from the strong patriarchal culture in society.

Therefore, victims of gender-based violence and violence against children need to receive protection in accordance with the principles of justice, truth, legal certainty, equality, and upholding human rights. This Regional Regulation regulates the Implementation of Protection for Victims of Gender-Based Violence and Children, particularly in terms of prevention and services, protection mechanisms, community participation, guidance, funding, and supervision.

6.7.rationale: The Indonesian source (Penjelasan Pasal 2 huruf a) lists non-discrimination grounds: "suku, agama, ras, golongan, jenis kelamin, etnis, budaya, bahasa, status hukum dan kondisi fisik maupun mental." This is a general equality clause; it does not specifically identify minority groups as a target group for tailored interventions, nor does it discuss outreach to isolated/minority communities beyond stating they must not be discriminated against. The judge treated the general non-discrimination list (ethnicity, religion, race, culture, language) as sufficient to mark the 'Minority groups' indicator Yes. If the indicator expects explicit mention of minority groups (or specific provisions for them), the judge’s reasoning is too permissive. The necessary information was in the retrieved passages and appears correctly translated, so this is an evaluation/thresholding error rather than RAG or translation.
